analysis.investment_thesis: Just Dial is a Reliance-backed local search business trading at 33.5x P/E with only 6.1% revenue CAGR over 9 years — structurally outside my SMILE framework at ₹4,675 Cr market cap. The profit story is distorted by treasury income on ₹4,000+ Cr investments, masking a mediocre core business fighting Google and IndiaMart.
key_strengths: Near debt-free (D/E 0.02) with massive ₹4,000+ Cr investment book generating ₹300+ Cr other income annually
74.15% promoter (Reliance Retail) holding gives strong corporate backing and distribution leverage for JD Mart B2B pivot
FCF has recovered strongly to ₹305 Cr in FY25 from ₹24 Cr trough in FY22, with 5/5 years OCF positive
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of just 6.1% over 9 years — far too slow for a multibagger; core local search faces existential pressure from Google and vertical platforms
ROE of 3.63% on ₹4,606 Cr equity base is deeply sub-par despite ₹584 Cr net profit — capital is not being deployed productively
Profitability heavily dependent on treasury/other income (₹305 Cr in FY24 alone); strip that out and operating business earns a fraction of reported profits
red_flags: Market cap ₹4,675 Cr — 4-5x outside my small-cap sweet spot; institutional money already present (FII 5.96% + DII 8.96%)
P/E 33.5x vs my preferred 8-15x entry range; unjustifiable for 6% revenue grower
EV/EBITDA of -3.06 signals the market is effectively buying a treasury fund with a struggling operating business attached
No transformation catalyst — JD Mart B2B pivot competes against established IndiaMart/TradeIndia; no visible inflection
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my SMILE lens, Just Dial fails on almost every criterion. At ₹4,675 Cr market cap, it is 4-5x above my sweet spot and is well-covered by institutions — the information asymmetry edge that creates multibaggers simply does not exist here. Revenue has grown at a paltry 6.1% CAGR over 9 years (₹668 Cr in FY16 to ₹1,142 Cr in FY25), which is below nominal GDP growth — this is not a business capturing a large underpenetrated market, it is one fighting for survival against Google Maps for local search. The forward P/E of 7.69x looks tempting but is misleading: the massive investment corpus (~₹4,000 Cr) built from the Reliance acquisition deal generates ₹300+ Cr in other income annually, inflating reported net profits far above what the operating business earns.

The Reliance Retail parentage (74.15% stake) is a double-edged sword. While it provides capital, distribution, and balance-sheet stability, it removes exactly what I look for — a hungry, independent promoter-founder with personal wealth tied to the outcome, making bold bets to 10x the business. The business had a near-death experience in FY22 (EBITDA crashed to ₹26 Cr) and has since recovered, but operating income of ₹675 Cr in FY25 vs EBITDA of ₹369 Cr suggests significant non-operating adjustments. ROE of 3.63% is structurally unacceptable; a business earning ₹584 Cr profit on ₹4,606 Cr equity should post ~12-13% ROE — the stated 3.63% signals either data inconsistency or prior year averaging against a massively inflated equity base from the Reliance deal. Either way, this is not a SMILE candidate. There are far better compounders in the ₹100-500 Cr market cap universe.
